tools.@searching: a line in the assistant's panel while it searches the notes; {query} is the words it searches for
tools.@reading: a line in the assistant's panel while it reads one note; {title} is the note's title

changes.@createNote: the heading of a change the assistant proposes, before the person allows it; {title} is the new note's title
changes.@createdNote: what the assistant did, after the person allowed it; {title} is the new note's title
changes.@editNote: the heading of a change the assistant proposes to an existing note; {title} is the note's title
changes.@editedNote: what the assistant did to an existing note; {title} is the note's title
changes.@addCards: the heading of a change the assistant proposes: adding flashcards to a note; {title} is the note's title
changes.@addedCards: what the assistant did: it added flashcards to a note; {title} is the note's title

labels.@inside: label of a detail of a proposed new note: the note it will be put inside (followed by that note's path)

undo.changedMessage: Taking the assistant’s change back puts the note as it was before it, so what was written in it after that would be lost too.

@open: tooltip and accessible name of the title bar button that shows or hides the assistant panel

mood.asleep: Asleep. Turn me on and we’ll begin.
mood.curious: Who goes there? Sign in and we’ll talk.
mood.thinking: I know that I know nothing. One moment.
mood.writing: Writing. Plato usually did this for me.
mood.dizzy: Something broke. Not me, I think.
mood.broke: Out of drachmas until next month.

@mood: one short, dry line in the assistant’s own voice, shown beside its face on the assistant’s page. He is drawn as Socrates and some lines nod to that (he lived about 2,400 years ago, was paid in drachmas, wrote nothing down himself: Plato did, and is known for saying he knew nothing); keep the joke, not the words. Each fits the face he is making: asleep (not turned on), curious (needs sign-in), idle, listening to the person type, thinking, reading notes, writing, asking for permission to make a change, bored after a long wait, scheming in the middle of a long task, flattered at being thanked, proud of something done, sad at being told no, embarrassed at a change taken back, dizzy after an error, broke (the month’s allowance is used up), and declining to answer

search.words: assistant chat ai ask help socrates

@search: search words (never shown) that also find the assistant in the Go To list of the search, separated by spaces

intro.can: Answer from your notes, make notes and flashcards, add assignments and events, and edit notes. It always shows a change and waits for you before making it.
intro.sends: Only what you ask, and the notes it reads for that request, go to the model through Thought Desk’s server and on to Anthropic, which keeps them for up to 30 days and does not train on them. Nothing is sent in the background.
intro.never: Delete anything for good, share anything, or touch sync or sign-in.
intro.@turnOn: button in the assistant panel that turns the assistant on for the first time

signedOut.text: The assistant needs an account, so its use can be counted fairly.

examples.@find: a suggested request in the empty assistant panel; clicking it starts the sentence in the input for the person to finish

composer.@placeholder: placeholder of the assistant’s message box; {name} is what the person calls the assistant
composer.@send: accessible name of the button that sends a message to the assistant
composer.@stop: button that stops the assistant while it is answering
composer.@allowance: a small line under the assistant’s message box; {percent} is a whole number from 0 to 100

@thinking: shown in the assistant panel while it has not started writing its answer

marks.@running: accessible name of the small spinner next to a step the assistant is running
marks.@done: accessible name of the check mark beside a finished step, and of a ticked task in an answer
marks.@notDone: a change the person did not allow; also the accessible name of an unticked task in an answer
marks.@couldnt: accessible name of the mark beside a step the assistant could not finish

change.@allow: button that lets the assistant make the change shown in the card
change.@decline: button that refuses the change shown in the card, next to “Allow”
change.@working: shown on a change card while the assistant is making the change
change.@open: button on a finished change that opens the note, assignment or event it made
change.@undo: button on a finished change that takes it back
change.@undone: shown on a change card after the person took the change back
change.@show: button that shows the preview of a change that was already decided
change.@hide: button that hides the preview of a change that was already decided
change.@now: label above the text as it is now, in a preview of an edit
change.@after: label above the text as it would be, in a preview of an edit
change.@adding: label above text the assistant would add, in a preview of an edit
change.@removing: label above text the assistant would remove, in a preview of an edit
change.@waiting: a bar above the assistant’s message box when changes wait for the person’s answer; {count} is how many
change.@allowAll: button in the bar of waiting changes that allows every one of them

notice.signedOut: Sign in to use the assistant.
notice.closed: The assistant isn’t open to this account yet.
notice.off: The assistant isn’t set up on this server yet.
notice.spent: You’ve used this month’s assistant allowance. It starts again next month.
notice.busy: The assistant is busy right now. Try again in a moment.
notice.fast: That was a bit quick. Try again in a moment.
notice.offline: No connection to the assistant. Check your internet and try again.
notice.cut: The answer was cut off for being too long.
notice.steps: It stopped after working for a long while. Ask it to continue if it wasn’t done.

settings.title: Assistant

settings.name: Its name
